_why: Provenance for the recordings in this folder, kept as data rather than
prose so a test can check it and so it still says what these bags were
if the bags themselves ever live only on the SSD. The bags are stored
through Git LFS; sha256 is what makes a copy on any disk verifiable
against the one the vehicle wrote.

session.question: does localization stay attached over the whole 0727 route
session.answer: yes - TRACKING for every driving sample of both runs

configuration.cluster_avoidance: run 1 on until 21:49, off afterwards; run 2 off
note: The discretionary guards were off because a band refusal or a
geofence trip would have ended the measurement while looking, from
outside a stationary chair, exactly like the lost fix it was meant
to detect. Suppressed guards were still evaluated and published as
WOULD_HOLD: on /waypoint_follower/status, which is in these bags.

measured_while_driving.state: TRACKING for all of them, both runs

known_excursion.when: 22:39:41-22:40:02, parked at the goal, 20 min after run 2 ended
reading: Nothing was driving. It is the one place all evening the fix came
near its gate, so the end of this route is its weakest geometry.

contains: Started with cluster avoidance ON and stopped at waypoint 349 for
14 minutes. Not localization: the cluster guard's bounding box
reported a diagonal wall as 0.69 m dead ahead when its nearest
point inside the corridor was 2.13 m. The follower was relaunched
with cluster avoidance off at 21:49 and the route completed.
This bag therefore holds both the defect and the recovery.

bags.run: second autonomous run, recorded end to end for video
contains: Clean run from waypoint 1, no obstacle stop, no intervention.
Also holds the parked excursion described in known_excursion,
which happens after the route is already DONE.

notes: Both bags were written .active because the stack was killed rather
than shut down, and were reindexed on the vehicle before transfer.
The sha256 above is of the reindexed bag, not the .active original.
/perception/objects_summary is the record the cluster-guard defect
has to be fixed against: it carries every object the tracker reported,
with its motion verdict, for both runs.
